title: I Walk Into Every Quarterly Meeting Wanting To Be Tony Robbins Heres What Actually Happens
author: Summer Mulder
summary: Mulder's honest reflection on quarterly meetings reveals the gap between leadership aspirations and what actually happens and works. Despite good intentions to inspire, empower, and transform team energy through a quarterly meeting, most end up becoming information transfers with limited real impact on people or culture. Mulder explores what actually works to make quarterly gatherings meaningful: clarity about purpose, vulnerability about challenges, and real dialogue instead of broadcast leadership theater. The lesson is that quarterly meetings are opportunities for connection and direction-setting.
points: Most quarterly meetings fail because they're designed as broadcasts instead of dialogues.
Leaders often walk in with unrealistic aspirations about transformation without clear structure.
Quarterly meetings work when they focus on clarity and connection, not inspiration.
Real dialogue and vulnerability from leadership makes quarterly meetings meaningful.
The best quarterly meetings are about listening and understanding, not performing.
Information can be an email; quarterly meetings need to be about dialogue.
